text:
Mirroring the unseen night sky above, pinpricks of bright indigo light scatter across the slime molds that wind downwards through cramped tunnels, 
lighting a path to depths unknown. The Traveler, gripping the weathered strap of their pack tightly at their shoulder once again questions whether this 
delve was worth the potential peril. With a conscious effort they try not to think of the untold tonnes of stone resting above their head, or the skittering 
sounds heard just outside the soft glow of the molds. Battling against the grip of fear, they step forward, one foot in front of the other.
In these depths, tracking the passage of time is a futility best not attempted, yet the Traveler notices changes as they descend. The usual labyrinth of 
passages and branching tunnels are met with tough fibrous white growths blockading entrances, further reinforcing only one path downward. Over 
time the white substance begins to wind entirely around the tunnels, timidly the Traveler touches it, relieved to find it firm to the touch and unlike much 
in this alkaline underground, not melting through their glove.
Jotting down notes in their journal, about this potential new building material, the quiet clicking of legs go unnoticed. Within the space of a heart beat 
the silence is shattered when an explosion of skittering legs pounds down the webbed walls, echoing with the promise of death. Before the dim lights could 
illuminate what was quickly approaching, the Traveler spins around and runs, not sparring a moment to regret missing the opportunity to document 
the creature, as absolute terror instead overwhelms them in their mad dash to escape back up to the light of day.
Through decades of unchecked growth in the hidden depths of the earth, the taurachni have grown to monumental sizes, securing 
miles of criss-crossing tunnels as their lair, funneling all manner of creatures into their web to feast. The taurachni prowl the caves as 
aggressive and unrivaled apex predators, their reinforced carapace and thick limbs allowing the creature to defend their lair against 
rivals arthropods that would seek to take them down. With such an excessively large size, many of the unique traits that arachnids 
have honed over millions have years have atrophied in this brute of a spider. Too heavy to hold itself to the ceilings, and too large to 
necessitate having a venomous bite to incapacitate larger prey, the arachnid instead acts like a rampaging beast, barreling into its 
prey, crushing and pummeling them into a broken waste and sucking up the pulped remains. In the rare instances when a nicalliath 
or dozens of desperate skith may attempt to slay the massive spider, the conflict can be felt shaking through the earth even those that 
stand on the surface above, may wonder if the earth is quaking, as the taurachni throws its considerable weight into the stone walls 
with jarring force. When the battle calms, and the beast sates its hunger, they enter long resting periods of torpor, awaiting the next 
telltale vibration of trapped creatures within their winding webbed tunnels.
Deep beneath the earth, life bloomed unlike ever before. Growing from a foundation of sulfur instead of sunlight, flora and fauna 
rose into new, almost alien manners. Those that grew strong and out competed the other creatures needed to be both versatile and 
ruthless, and few can match the arachnids in this regard having been already competing in an evolutionary arms race with arthropods 
for hundreds of millions of years. Elsewhere above ground, only the avians had ever kept arachnids from rising to the top of any food 
chain and, the Umbrawells, within their endless dark tunnels of burgeoning life became an opportunity like no other for the quickly 
adapting arachnids to rise, and eventually lead to the colossal juggernaut that is the taurachni.
 
While spiders inhabit countless crevices throughout each and every subterranean environment that worms through Sol'Kesh, only 
the deepest and widest spaces can harbor an infestation of taurachni. Larger than any other arachnid, these apex predators hunt in 
vast webs with only a rare few of them ever reaching adulthood. Younger and smaller taurachni venture out to shape their own nest, 
only to be slain by the highly competitive predators that prowl the darkness. First and foremost, the vaulted caverns that rise up the 
Splitspine mountains feature the most taurachni, these caverns becoming essentially rebuilt as the beasts cordon off tunnels with 
their thick webbing and break through others to allow their bulk to pass. Many of their kin split off and ventured east into the tunnels 
that lead to the Stoanhalls, nesting in cliff face caverns open to the sky, pouncing on nesting skyelarx that get too close. Further south, 
where even the crash of the ocean cannot be heard in the subterranean lakes that run deeply into the Drowned Hollows, through the 
thick application of their webbing they are able to shore up sunken tunnels and venture beneath the waterline. Here taurachni contend 
with esslinter and daellash, both eels having little chance to escape the armored behemoth once they worm too deeply into its nest. 
Taurachni are not merely a specter of death within the Umbrawells, and many creatures live within their webs, as the spider pays little 
attention to small pests not worth the effort of crushing. Their webbing not only provide structured layers in many vast open caverns, 
but also hosts bacteria, fungi and a multitude of insects that all live within its unique ecology.
Travelers set on delving into the domain of the taurachni must know that they are willingly stepping into a trap. While the webs prove 
to be hard as stone out on the periphery of their lair, the closer one gets funneled into the center, the more supple and sensitive the 
webs become, and vibrate with the step of incoming prey. With a slow metabolism, the taurachni spends much of its time feasting 
and digesting crushed and captured prey, but at the slightest vibration they quickly travel their lair to investigate. With a speed and 
silence one would not expect for a creature of its size, it rushes down pitch back paths, knowing each turn and step of its domain 
instinctively with only a rumbling tremor in the webbing to forewarn of its approach. If a Traveler is fortunate enough to heed these 
subtle warnings, they must be either willing to fight to the death, or find themselves any small crevice that the webbing failed to cover, 
and hope to hide from the fast approaching master of the lair.
